title: Zero-shot design of drug-binding proteins via neural iterative selection−expansion
methods: autoregressive sequence and side-chain dihedral decoding
iterative selection-expansion (coordinate ascent on a joint distribution)
rigid-body ligand docking (CARPdock) and COMBS/van der Mers placement
data_sources: Protein Data Bank protein-ligand co-crystal structures

data_scope.training_data: PDB protein-ligand co-crystal structures; exact count not stated in the main text; processed REDUCE-protonated training set released on Zenodo
data_scope.ligand_encoder_pretraining: SPICE v2.0.1 (drug-like molecules and peptides, quantum-chemistry atom properties), encoder frozen during sequence-design training
data_scope.held_out_benchmarks: streptavidin fold held out by sequence/structure/evolutionary similarity (up to 94% binding-site recovery in top-25 of 10,000 designs); PiB / PDB 8TN6 held out from LASErMPNN and RFAA (74% binding-site, 80% core recovery; native ranked 4th of 1,001)
data_scope.scaffold_libraries: 40 AF2-validated four-helix bundles (exatecan); 50 Boltz-2-validated NTF2 backbones (apixaban, reused from prior published work for head-to-head comparison)
data_scope.sampling_volume: 1,000 LASErMPNN sequences per selected structure per NISE round, top 3 structures carried forward; benchmark trajectory n = 1,500 designs per iteration (500 in round 1) over 35 rounds; 30,000 sequences from 10,000 CARPdock apixaban poses
data_scope.experimental_tests: exatecan: 4 NISE designs tested, 4 bound (100%), vs 16 COMBS-Rosetta designs with 3 monomeric binders; apixaban: 6 NISE designs tested, 5 bound (83%)
data_scope.affinities: EPIC Kd = 0.12 uM; EPIC(Q51N) 8.0 nM; EPIC(M97L) 7.4 nM; EPIC(Q51N/M97L) 1.2 nM; anti-design control EPIC(G104M) 57 uM; HSA 43 uM; APEX-apixaban Kd = 80 pM (95% CI 54-122 pM)
data_scope.compute: typical 14-iteration NISE trajectory approx. 5 h on four NVIDIA A6000 GPUs
data_scope.functional_assay: >99% of exatecan retained in the bioactive ring-closed form for at least 50 h in PBS pH 7.4 at 295 K, including with 500 uM human serum albumin
data_scope.not_reported: number of PDB training complexes, held-out test-set size, and any in vivo or pharmacokinetic data

core_conclusion: Closing the loop between two reciprocal neural networks - a ligand-aware graph sequence designer (LASErMPNN) and a protein-ligand co-structure predictor (RFAA or Boltz-2) - enables zero-shot design of small-molecule binding proteins. The NISE algorithm climbs the joint distribution P(sequence, structure, ligand conformation) instead of following a physics-based energy function, yielding binders to exatecan (4/4, 100%) and apixaban (5/6, 83%) with affinities down to 1.2 nM and 80 pM, roughly 70-fold and 10,000-fold tighter than the previous best methods, and a designed binder that protects exatecan's labile lactone ring for over 50 hours.
why_it_matters: Turns small-molecule binder design from a high-throughput screening problem into a computational one: 6 designs tested versus 9,024 for the prior method on identical backbones and target. Shows that the second neural network, not a Rosetta energy function, is what makes the loop optimize; delivers purely computational affinity maturation (neural proofreading, 100x gain), crystallographic confirmation at 2.0-2.2 A, a functional drug-stabilizing reagent, and fully open code, notebooks and data.
why_nature: A long-standing barrier - zero-shot de novo small-molecule binder design - is broken rather than incrementally improved; the apixaban experiment is a strict head-to-head on previously published backbones so the gain cannot be attributed to a better starting point; the paper couples a probabilistic argument (coordinate ascent on a joint distribution) to architecture, wet-lab affinities, two crystal structures and a functional hydrolysis-protection assay; generality is demonstrated across two drugs, two folds and two interchangeable structure predictors; and there are immediate translational hooks (a cheap apixaban antidote candidate, an ADC-payload carrier) plus full open-source release.
added_value_to_my_research: Learned selection-expansion controller -> principled search schedule and stopping rule for R2SFCA catchment design and EV-charging siting
Confidence calibration audit of pLDDT-style surrogates -> calibration-first explainable-ML protocol for spatial accessibility prediction
Neural proofreading as single-site counterfactual scan -> minimal-intervention explainability for facility add/remove/relocate in access networks
Positive/negative design gap objective -> efficiency-vs-equity trade-off recast as an explicit specificity gap for spatial interventions

Zero-shot generalization benchmarking and FAIR release -> unseen-region evaluation protocol for fine-tuned geospatial foundation models, plus a health-geography study of access to anticoagulant reversal
